title: PostgreSQL Performance Engineering: Plans, Indexes & Pagination
concept: Make slow PostgreSQL queries fast with evidence, not guesses: measure a baseline, read EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS), understand scans, joins and row estimates, design composite, covering and expression indexes, replace N+1 loops and OFFSET pages, and change indexes on a live database without blocking it. Graded exercises run on SQLite query plans.
description: An advanced course for backend developers whose queries worked fine until the data grew. Every lesson starts from a slow endpoint or report on the CodeDev learning platform - a progress page that takes seconds, a submissions feed whose deep pages crawl and repeat rows, a login lookup that stopped using its index after a deploy, an AI-generated composite index in the wrong column order - and fixes it the way production engineers do: measure, read the plan, change one thing, measure again. You read real-looking PostgreSQL plans, estimate selectivity from statistics, design indexes for the query pattern and weigh their write cost, rewrite N+1 loops and correlated reports into set-based SQL, paginate with keyset cursors, and plan index changes around locks. 11 lessons with evidence-based quizzes and hands-on SQL and Python challenges graded on results and query plans.

lessons.title: Measure before you tune: baselines, percentiles & pg_stat_statements
How to read a PostgreSQL plan: EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)
Sequential scan or index: how the planner reaches the rows
Estimated vs actual rows: statistics & selectivity
Composite & covering indexes: why column order matters
Join strategies and the N+1 query problem
Deep pages: when OFFSET gets slow and drifts
Locks, long transactions & index changes without downtime
